questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a cash book in accounting?

options.text: To record all cash and bank transactions.

questions.explanation: The cash book is used to record all cash and bank transactions, making it an essential part of the books of original entry.

distractorRationale.a: Credit transactions are recorded in other journals, not the cash book.
distractorRationale.b: Inventory levels are tracked using inventory records, not the cash book.
distractorRationale.d: Profit and loss calculations are done in the income statement, not the cash book.

questions.stem: In a three-column cash book, what does the third column represent?
questions.explanation: The third column in a three-column cash book is used to record discounts allowed and received.

distractorRationale.a: Cash transactions are recorded in the cash column.
distractorRationale.b: Bank transactions are recorded in the bank column.
distractorRationale.d: Credit transactions are not recorded in the cash book.

questions.stem: Which of the following transactions would require a contra entry in the cash book?

options.text: Deposit of ₦2,000 cash into the bank

questions.explanation: A contra entry occurs when cash is deposited into or withdrawn from the bank, affecting both the cash and bank columns.

distractorRationale.a: Cash sales affect only the cash column.
distractorRationale.b: Payments to suppliers affect only the cash or bank column.
distractorRationale.d: Receipts from debtors affect only the cash column.

questions.stem: If a business records a cash sale of ₦10,000 and a bank deposit of ₦4,000 in a two-column cash book, what is the cash balance?
questions.explanation: The cash balance is calculated by subtracting the bank deposit from the cash sales: ₦10,000 - ₦4,000 = ₦6,000.

distractorRationale.d: This option reflects only the bank deposit.
